source_text: Quibus duobus dominis neget posse seruiri, quia alterum offendi sit necesse alterum defendi, ipse declarat, deum proponens et mamonam. proinde mamonam quem intellegi uelit, si interpretem non habes, ab ipso potes discere. admonens enim nos de saecularibus suffragia nobis prospicere amicitiarum secundum serui illius exemplum, qui ab actu summotus dominicos debitores diminutis cautionibus releuat in subsidium sibi: et ego, inquit, dico uobis, facite uobis amicos de mamona iniustitiae, de nummo scilicet, de \' quo et seruus ille. iniustitiae enim auctorem et dominatorem totius saeculi nummum scimus omnes. cui famulatam uidens Pharisaeorum cupiditatem ammentauit hanc sententiam: non potestis deo seruire et mamonae. inridebant denique Pharisaei pecuniae cupidi, quod intellexissent scilicet mamonam de nummo dictum, ne quia existimet in mamona creatorem intellegendum et Christum a creatoris illos seruitute reuocasse.. quid nunc? potius ex hoc disce unum a Christo deum ostensum. duos enim dominos nominauit, deum et mamonam, crea. torem et nummum: denique non potestis deo seruire, utique ei, cui uidebantur seruire, et mamonam, cui magis destinabantur. quodsi ipse alium se ageret, non duos dominos, sed tres demonstrasset — et creator enim dominus, quia deus, et utique magis dominus quam mamonas magisque homini obseruandus, qua magis dominus —; quale est enim, ut qui mamonam dominum dixerat et cum domino iunxerat uero, ipsum dominum taceret, id est deum creatorem? aut numquid tacendo eo concessit seruiendum ei esse, si solummodo sibi et mamonae negauit posse seruiri? ita cum unum deum ponit, nominaturus et creatorem, si alius esset ipse, creatorem nominauit quem [dominum] sine alio [deo non] posuit. et illud itaque relucebit, quomodo dictum sit: (si) in mamona iniusto fideles non extitistis, quod uerum est quis uobis credet? in nummo scilicet iniusto, non in creatore, quem et Marcion iustum facit, et: si in alieno fideles inuenti non estis, meum quis dabit uobis? alienum enim debet esse a semis dei quod iniustum est. creator autem quomodo alienus erat Pharisaeis, proprius deus Iudaicae gentis? si ergo haec non cadunt in creatorem, sed in mamonam, \'quis uobis credet quod uerius est\'? et \'quis uobis dabit quod meum est\'? non potest quasi ali{en)us dixisse de alterius dei gratia. tunc enim uideretur ita dixisse, si eos in creatorem, non in mamonam infideles notando per creatoris mentionem distinctione se fecisset dei alterius, non commissuri suam ueritatem infidelibus creatoris, t quoniam tunc alterius uideri potest, si non ad hoc proponatur, ut a re, de qua agitur, separetur. Si autem et iustificantes se coram hominibus Pharisaei spem mercedis in homine ponebant, illo eos sensu increpabat, quo et propheta Hieremias: miser homo, qui spem habet in homine. si et adicit: scit autem deus corda uestra, illius dei uim commemorabat, (qui) lucernam se pronuntiarat scrutantem renes et corda. si superbiam tangit: quod elatum est apud homines perosum est deo, Esaiam ponit ante oculos: dies enim domini Sabaoth in omnem contumeliosum et superbum, in omnem sublimem et elatum, et humiliabuntur. Possum iam colligere, cur tanto aeuo deus Marcionis fuerit in occulto. expectabat, opinor, donec haec omnia disceret a creatore. didicit igitur usque ad Iohannis tempora atque ita exinde processit adnuntiare regnum dei dicens: lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem; ex quo regnum dei adnuntiatur. quasi non et nos limitem quendam agnoscamus Iohannem constitutum inter uetera et noua, ad quem desineret Iudaismus et a quo inciperet Christianismus, non tamen, ut ab alia uirtute facta sit sedatio legis et prophetarum et initiatio euangelii, in quo est dei regnum.\' [Christus ipse.] nam id si probauimus, et uetera transitura et noua successura praedicari a creatore, si et Iohannes antecursor et praeparator ostenditur uiarum domini euangelium\', superducturi et regnum dei promulgaturi, et ex hoc iam, quod Iohannes uenit, ipse erit Christus qui Iohannem erit subsecutus ut antecursorem; et, si desierunt uetera et coeperunt ! noua interstite Iohanne, non erit mirum quod ex dispositione est creatoris, ut unde(unde) magis probetur ** quam ex legis et prophetarum in Iohannem occasu et exinde ortu regni dei. transeat igitur caelum et terra citius, sicut et lex et: prophetae, quam unus apexuerborum domini-nerbum enim, inquit Esaias, dei nostri manet in aeuum —: nam quoniam in Esaia iam tunc Christus, sermo scilicet et spiritus creatoris, Iohannem praedicarat — uocem clamantis in deserto: parate uiam domini — in hoc uenturum, ut legis et] prophetarum ordo exinde cessaret, per adimpletionem, non per destructionem, et regnum dei a Christo adnuntiaretur, I ideo subtexuit facilius elementa transitura quam uerba sua,\' confirmans hoc quoque, quod de Iohanne dixerat, non praeterisse.
pass_a_gloss: To whom He says that two masters cannot be served, because it is necessary to offend one and defend the other, He Himself declares, setting forth God and mammon. Therefore, mammon, which He wishes to be understood, if you do not have an interpreter, you can learn from Him. For, admonishing us to look out for worldly friendships according to the example of that servant, who, having been removed from office, relieves his master's debtors by diminishing their securities for his own benefit: and I, He says, tell you, make friends for yourselves from mammon of injustice, from money, of course, from which also that servant. For we know that money is the author and ruler of all worldly injustice. Seeing the covetousness of the Pharisees, He strengthened this statement: you cannot serve God and mammon. Finally, the Pharisees, who were greedy for money, ridiculed, because they understood, of course, that mammon was spoken of in terms of money, not because they thought that the creator should be understood in mammon and that Christ had recalled them from the service of that creator. What now? Rather, learn from this that one God is shown by Christ. For He named two masters, God and mammon, the creator and money: finally, you cannot serve God, certainly to Him, whom they seemed to serve, and mammon, to whom they were more devoted. But if He Himself were acting as another, He would have shown not two masters, but three — and the creator is indeed the Lord, because He is God, and certainly a greater Lord than mammon, and more to be obeyed by man, because He is a greater Lord —; what kind of thing is it, that He who said mammon was a master and joined it with the Lord, would be silent about the Lord Himself, that is, the creator God? Or did He, by being silent about it, concede that it should be served, if only He denied that it could be served along with mammon? Thus, when He sets forth one God, He names the creator, if He Himself were another, He named the creator, whom He set forth as Lord without another God. And that statement will also become clear, how it was said: if you have not been faithful in mammon of injustice, what is true, who will trust you? Certainly in unjust money, not in the creator, whom even Marcion makes just, and: if you have not been found faithful in what is another's, who will give you what is mine? For what is unjust should be alien to the semi-god. But how was the creator alien to the Pharisees, the proper God of the Jewish people? If, therefore, these things do not fall upon the creator, but upon mammon, 'who will trust you what is truer?' And 'who will give you what is mine?' He cannot have said this as if it were alien, as if it were from the grace of another god. For then He would seem to have said this, if He had noted them as unfaithful in the creator, not in mammon, by mentioning the creator, making a distinction, not entrusting His truth to the unfaithful of the creator, since then it could seem to be from another, if it were not proposed in order to separate it from the thing being discussed. But if the Pharisees, justifying themselves before men, placed their hope of reward in men, He rebuked them with the same sense in which the prophet Jeremiah said: woe to the man who puts his hope in man. And if He adds: but God knows your hearts, He commemorated the power of that God, who declared Himself to be a lamp searching the kidneys and hearts. If He touches on pride: what is exalted among men is an abomination to God, He sets Isaiah before their eyes: for the day of the Lord of hosts will be upon every arrogant and haughty one, and they will be humbled. I can now gather why the God of Marcion was in hiding for so long. He was waiting, I think, until all these things were learned from the creator. Therefore, He learned up to the time of John and thus proceeded to announce the kingdom of God, saying: the law and the prophets were until John; from whom the kingdom of God is announced. As if we also do not recognize a certain boundary established by John between the old and the new, at which Judaism ceased and Christianity began, not, however, that the cessation of the law and the prophets and the initiation of the gospel, in which is the kingdom of God, was made by another virtue. For if we have proven this, that the old things are passing away and the new things are succeeding, as proclaimed by the creator, and John is shown to be the forerunner and preparer of the ways of the Lord, and the gospel is to be brought and the kingdom of God is to be proclaimed, and from this, now that John has come, He Himself will be Christ, who will follow John as a forerunner; and if the old things have ceased and the new things have begun, with John in between, it will not be surprising that this is from the disposition of the creator, so that it may be proven more than from the passing away of the law and the prophets in John and from then on the rising of the kingdom of God. Therefore, let heaven and earth pass away more quickly, just as the law and the prophets, than one dot of the Lord's words — for the word of our God remains forever —; for since in Isaiah, Christ, namely the speech and spirit of the creator, had already predicted John, saying: a voice crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord — in this, that the order of the law and the prophets would cease from then on, through fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ —, He therefore wove in more easily that the elements would pass away than His own words, confirming also what He had said about John, that it had not passed away.

choices.why: The Latin word 'mamona' is translated to 'wealth' or 'riches' in this context.
The Latin word 'deus' is translated to 'God' in this context.

bible_refs.note: Non potestis deo seruire et mamonae
si in alieno fideles non estis, quis uobis dabit quod meum est?

pass_b_english: Jesus tells us two masters cannot be served, because you must offend one to defend the other. He makes the point by naming God and mammon. So what is mammon? If you lack an interpreter, learn it from Jesus himself. He warns us to secure our future through worldly friendships, following the example of the steward who, once fired, cut his master's debtors' bills to buy himself a safety net. 'I tell you,' he says, 'make friends for yourselves with the mammon of injustice — that is, money, the very stuff that steward used.' We all know money is the author and ruler of all worldly injustice. When Jesus saw the Pharisees' greed, he drove the point home: 'You cannot serve God and mammon' (Luke 16:13). The money-loving Pharisees sneered, because they understood he was talking about cash, not that the Creator was the mammon from which Christ had recalled them. So learn this instead: Christ reveals one God. He names two masters — God and mammon, the Creator and money. 'You cannot serve God' means that very God they claimed to serve, and mammon, the one they actually served. If Jesus were a different god, he would have presented three masters, not two — for the Creator is Lord because he is God, a greater Lord than mammon, and more to be obeyed because he is greater. What sense does it make for the one who called mammon a master and paired it with the Lord to then fall silent about the Lord himself, the Creator God? Or did his silence concede that the Creator should be served, just not alongside mammon? When he sets up one God, he names the Creator. If Jesus were another god, he just named the Creator as Lord without any other god. This also clarifies the saying: 'If you have not been faithful in the mammon of injustice, who will trust you with true riches?' (Luke 16:11). That means unjust money, not the Creator — whom even Marcion calls just. And: 'If you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?' The unjust must be alien to the demiurge. But how was the Creator alien to the Pharisees, the proper God of the Jewish nation? If these words target mammon, not the Creator, then 'who will trust you with what is truer?' and 'who will give you what is mine?' Jesus could not speak as if the true riches belonged to another god's grace. He would only sound that way if he had charged them with unfaithfulness to the Creator rather than to mammon, invoking the Creator to distinguish his own god — not entrusting his truth to the Creator's unfaithful — since that would make his truth seem alien if it were not meant to separate them from the matter at hand. The Pharisees justified themselves before men and pinned their hope of reward on men. Jesus rebuked them in the same spirit as Jeremiah: 'Woe to the man who trusts in man.' When he adds, 'But God knows your hearts,' he invokes the power of that God who called himself a lamp searching kidneys and hearts. When he strikes at pride — 'What is exalted among men is an abomination to God' — he holds up Isaiah: 'The day of the Lord of hosts comes against every arrogant and haughty one, and they will be humbled.' I can now see why Marcion's god stayed hidden for so long. He was waiting, I suppose, until he learned all this from the Creator. So he learned up to John's time, then launched his announcement: 'The Law and the Prophets were until John; from him the kingdom of God is proclaimed.' As if we don't also recognize John as the boundary between old and new, where Judaism ends and Christianity begins — not as if the Law's cessation and the Gospel's start came from a different power. If we have proven that the old passes and the new succeeds by the Creator's decree, and John is shown as the forerunner and preparer of the Lord's ways, to bring the Gospel and proclaim the kingdom of God — then from John's arrival, Jesus himself is the Christ who follows John as forerunner. And if the old ceased and the new began with John in between, it is no surprise this came from the Creator's plan, so that it stands proven even more than by the Law and Prophets' sunset in John and the kingdom's rise thereafter. Let heaven and earth pass away sooner than one dot of the Lord's words — for 'the word of our God stands forever' — because in Isaiah, Christ, the Word and Spirit of the Creator, had already foretold John: 'A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord' — so that the order of the Law and Prophets would cease from then on through fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ. That is why he stitched in more easily that the elements would pass away than his own words, confirming that what he said about John had not failed.
